chunks: A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida' (peace be upon him) about the veil of the free women in the presence of the eunuchs. He (the Imam) said, 'They would enter upon the daughters of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and they would not veil themselves.' I asked, 'Were they free?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'So do the free ones veil themselves in their presence?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.قِنَاع: Veil or head covering worn by women
key_terms.يَتَقَنَّعْنَ: They veil themselves (verb form of qina')

ai.seo_question: Do free women need to wear a veil in front of eunuchs according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of hijab by distinguishing between free men and eunuchs, ruling that the latter are not considered 'free men' for the purpose of requiring a veil. This establishes a nuanced legal precedent where the requirement for covering is tied to the specific status of the observer, reflecting the practical social dynamics of the time. The ruling underscores the principle that hijab obligations are context-dependent rather than absolute in all private interactions.
